picked.t: Roche Vietnam funds clean water, rural bridge projects through employee donations
picked.body: The projects were funded through Roche Children's Walk program, an annual employee fundraising initiative launched globally in 2003 and introduced in Vietnam in 2008. Nearly 300 Roche employees across Vietnam participated in fundraising activities in 2026, including charity garage sales and direct donations. Within the 2026 program, a dedicated walk day was organized for employees and their families in Hanoi, Da Nang and Ho Chi Minh City to encourage community involvement and strengthen connections among staff. Funds raised from the program support two Roche’s long-term community initiatives: providing safe drinking water in schools and building bridges in remote areas to improve transportation and local trade. . In early October, Roche Vietnam partnered with VinaCapital Foundation (VCF) and the Vinh Long Department of Education and Training to donate a water filtration system to Hoa Thuan A Primary School in Hoa Thuan Ward, Vinh Long Province. The system provides filtered drinking water for students and school staff. Since partnering with VCF in 2022, Roche Vietnam has supported the installation of 13 school water filtration systems in provinces including Dak Lak, Quang Ngai, Ben Tre and Vinh Long. The systems have benefited nearly 6,000 students, teachers and school staff, according to the company. On Oct. 16, Roche Vietnam and Hope Foundation inaugurated Hope Bridge No. 457 in Hoa Dinh 1 Hamlet, Phong Hoa Commune, Dong Thap Province. Measuring 24 meters long and 3.5 meters wide, the bridge replaces an old, narrow structure that had deteriorated and raised safety concerns. The new bridge is expected to provide a safer route to school for children and improve transportation for residents. The project marks the fifth bridge Roche Vietnam has supported through its "Bridging to Future" initiative with Hope Foundation. Four previous projects were carried out in the Mekong Delta and Son La Province. Ricky He, general manager of Roche Vietnam, said access to clean water and safe transportation directly affects children's health, education and daily lives. "Essential needs such as clean drinking water or safe travel conditions directly impact the health, learning, and daily life of children," he said. "Through the Roche Children's Walk program, we hope to turn employee contributions into concrete impact, while partnering with organizations to implement projects aligned with local practical needs, thereby creating long-term values for the community." Roche Vietnam said it would continue working with VinaCapital Foundation and Hope Foundation on projects addressing local needs in healthcare, education and improving quality of life . Founded in Basel, Switzerland, in 1896, Roche operates in more than 150 countries through its Diagnostics and Pharmaceuticals divisions, developing healthcare products and solutions across areas including oncology, infectious diseases and immunology. Learn more at the company's Roche Diagnostics website or Roche Vietnam website . Roche Children's Walk is an annual employee fundraising initiative that supports projects to improve children's access to education, healthcare and essential services. Launched globally in 2003 and introduced in Vietnam in 2008, the program funds initiatives including school water filtration systems and rural transportation infrastructure.

picked.t: Vietnamese man gets life in prison for killing neighbor in Canada in feud over barbecue smoke
picked.body: Ontario Superior Court Justice Kenneth Campbell on Oct. 26 sentenced Khoa Tran, 36, to life with no chance of parole for 16 years for the second-degree murder of filmmaker Reeyaz Habib, 53, Global News reported. Tran's wife, Quynh (Isabelle) Nguyen, 30, had been convicted of being an accessory after the fact to manslaughter and of offering an indignity to a dead body. A jury found the couple guilty on June 3, when their bail was revoked. After enhanced credit for 146 days in pre-sentence custody, Nguyen has five years and four-and-a-half months left to serve. Campbell rejected the defense's proposal of a conditional sentence for Nguyen, two years less a day under house arrest followed by probation, as entirely unfit and in no way proportionate to the gravity of her offenses, calling her actions "truly despicable." Her lawyer, Tyler Smith, had argued that because Nguyen, a permanent resident, is not a Canadian citizen, a custodial sentence over six months would mean almost immediate deportation to Vietnam. Prosecutors had asked for 18 years before Tran could apply for parole and four to six years for Nguyen, while Tran's defense sought 12 to 13 years, CBC News reported. Second-degree murder carries an automatic life sentence, with parole ineligibility of 10 to 25 years. In June 2023, Tran and Nguyen owned a main-floor condo in a townhouse complex on Western Battery Road in Toronto's Liberty Village neighborhood, where Linh Hua, a longtime friend of the couple who had come from Vietnam, was staying with them. Habib, who lived alone, had the unit directly above. Habib, an alumnus of the Canadian Film Centre, had left a 15-year career on Bay Street, Toronto's financial district, to pursue filmmaking, the center said after his death. During the five-week trial, the court heard that smoke from Tran's barbecue drifted up into Habib's windows and that Habib repeatedly told Tran he did not want it in his unit. Prosecutors argued the dispute escalated after Habib threatened to go to the condo board to have Tran removed for infractions. Habib was killed in his home in the early hours of June 6, 2023. Neighbors heard screams from the direction of his unit, and before his body was discovered, one saw Tran leave it, lock the door and go back to his own. Habib's decomposing body was found on June 8, 2023, in a trash compactor in an underground garbage dumpster, wrapped in blankets and taped up with handles. Handwritten notes attached to it described the contents as trash, and one carried Tran's fingerprint, Campbell said. Had the compactor's operator not found it, the judge said, the body would likely never have been found. The duct-tape handles carried DNA from Habib, Tran and Nguyen. Habib was reported missing on June 9, before police had identified the body. Officers found blankets nailed over his window and the home carefully cleaned, and surveillance cameras had captured Tran throwing Habib's bike and computer into a nearby dumpster. Police announced Tran's arrest on June 30, 2023, on charges of indignity to a human body and obstruction of justice, CTV News reported. A second-degree murder charge followed in November that year. A forensic pathologist could not determine a cause of death because of the decomposition but testified that Habib had 35 external injuries, 24 of them inflicted before death, and internal injuries consistent with being beaten to death or strangled. Tran, a software developer, testified at trial that he threw away Habib's bicycle out of anger but had nothing to do with his death. Campbell found elements of planning, as Nguyen knew of her husband's plan to go upstairs and kill Habib that night. The couple had Hua sleep in their bedroom instead of on the living room mattress where she normally slept, so that Tran could work in the living room. When Hua heard loud footsteps and someone yelling for help upstairs around 3 a.m., Nguyen told her to ignore the noises and go back to sleep, saying Habib was likely filming. "Of course, these comments were nonsense. They had discussed what to say so she would not worry," Campbell said. Nguyen also told Hua to tell police, if they asked, that all three had slept in the bedroom, creating an alibi for Tran. The judge said Tran killed Habib to end his "consistent and bothersome interference" over the barbecue and to stop him from telling the condo board that a third person was living with the couple against the rules. "The killing of Mr. Habib was a senseless and selfish act by Mr. Tran," Campbell said. He was equally scathing about Nguyen, saying she not only helped dispose of the body but tried over an extended period to help her husband avoid arrest and prosecution. "These were callous and selfish acts taken to shield and protect her husband, the murderer," he said. Campbell said neither had expressed any remorse or regret, though Nguyen had addressed the court at the sentencing hearing: "I just want to say I am sorry to take the court time and money. I fee

picked.t: 베트남, 홍콩 제치고 ‘아시아 최고 크루즈 여행지’ 선정…월드크루즈어워즈
picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남이 쟁쟁한 후보를 제치고 올해 아시아 최고의 크루즈 여행지에 선정됐다. 베트남이 해당 부문을 수상한 것은 이번이 처음이다. 베트남은 최근 자메이카에서 열린 제6회 '2026년 월드크루즈어워즈(World Cruise Awards)’에서 ‘아시아 최고의 크루즈 여행지(Asia's Best Cruise Destination)’에 이름을 올렸다. 베트남과 함께 후보로 오른 국가는 한국과 일본, 싱가폴, 태국 등 9개국으로 이로써 베트남은 홍콩의 2연패를 저지하고, 수상의 영예를 안았다. 해당 부문은 지난 2021년 신설된 뒤, 싱가포르가 2연속 수상하고, 2023년에는 필리핀, 2024년과 2025년은 홍콩이 수상한 바 있다. 베트남의 크루즈 투어는 북부의 석회암 섬을 누비는 여정부터 남부 메콩강 삼각주의 강 여행까지 다채롭게 구성돼 있다. 하롱베이에서는 석회암 봉우리 사이를 항해하며, 하룻밤을 보낸 뒤, 밤에는 정박해 주변 섬을 바라보며 아침을 맞을 수 있다. 베트남관광청에 따르면, 투어 일정에는 선상 생활과 더불어 카약 타기와 동굴 탐방이 프로그램에 자주 포함되며, 선내에서는 쿠킹클래스와 오징어 낚시를 즐길 수 있다. 베트남관광청은 “메콩강 삼각주 크루즈는 지역민들의 강변 생활을 가까이서 볼 수 있는 여행”이라며 “관광객들은 야자나무가 늘어선 강둑과 마을을 지나며, 배에서 내려 현지 시장과 소도시를 둘러보거나 열대 과일을 맛볼 수 있다”고 설명하고 있다. 이 밖에도 베트남은 이번 시상식에서 베트남은 '세계 최고의 리버 크루즈 여행지(World's Best River Cruise Destination)'에 선정됐으며, 하롱크루즈항(Ha Long Cruise Port)은 ‘아시아 최고의 크루즈 터미널(Asia's Best Cruise Terminal’로 뽑혔다.

picked.t: Vietnam coffee king’s eldest son becomes deputy CEO of mother’s company
picked.body: Dang Le Trung Nguyen’s new position is "a milestone in his growth journey and a continuation of the family business," his mother Le Hoang Diep Thao, founder of TNI Group, which also produces coffee, said in a recent Facebook post. Nguyen, 28, is the eldest son of Vu and Thao, who divorced in 2019. They had two sons and two daughters together. Nguyen rarely appears in public. In late 2021, he and his younger brother, Dang Le Binh Nguyen, attended a ceremony to honor Vietnamese robusta coffee with a world record. Vu, dubbed Vietnam’s "coffee king," founded Trung Nguyen Group in 1996 and together with Thao transformed it into one of the biggest coffee producers in Vietnam. Following their divorce , a court ruling in 2020 awarded Vu the majority stake and control over Trung Nguyen Group and gave Thao VND1.32 trillion in cash and assets. This meant Thao was no longer involved in Trung Nguyen Group. She continued to lead her company TNI Corporation, which was previously Trung Nguyen International established in 2008 in Singapore to handle Trung Nguyen Group’s exports.
